items.title: Jean Bach interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: So she introduced me to a man named Matthew Seig, and you’ll see his credit on the end of the film. He’s my co-producer now.

ctx.x: Like the music rights, which is the worst, and a lot of other stuff. Stills — I thought I’d just borrow some stills from photographers who are friends of mine, and they all wanted © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -13-

$200 and stuff, it was terrible. I was filming people, I got a camera crew, and when I was able to locate people who are still alive who’d been there that day, I would do what you and I are doing and have a conversation. And I was well into it when Catherine Altman, who is married to Robert Altman, the great film maker, she’s one of my best friends. And she said, “Jean, I really think you could use some professional help.” Well I was a little annoyed. I thought, wait a minute, Catherine, I’m doing this. I thought…
Yes. We’ve been thinking about that same subject ourselves.
